title: German Grammar Review — B1 to C2
scope: Grammar only: morphology, syntax, verb forms, case, word order and sentence combining. Vocabulary, idioms and pronunciation are handled elsewhere.
sources: telc Grammatiktraining Deutsch für B2 — official table of contents
telc Grammatiktraining Deutsch für A1–B1 — official table of contents (Probekapitel)
Cornelsen Grammatik aktiv B2/C1 — chapter index
telc Deutsch C1 and C2 Übungstest format tables
CEFR Companion Volume 2020 — linguistic competence and propositional precision scales
caveats: No exam provider publishes a topic-by-topic grammar syllabus for C1 or C2. Goethe explicitly declines to fix a grammar or vocabulary inventory at those levels, so the C1 and C2 lists are inferred from coursebook canons and task formats.
Providers disagree on level placement. Topics marked provider_split are contested; the note gives the split.
ÖSD specifications could not be retrieved in usable form, so no ÖSD claims are made.

topics.covers: verbfirst in the main clause, verb-second with the conjugated verb, verb-last in the subordinate clause.

topics.topic_en: Irregular verbs in the present tense
topics.covers: nehmen, du nimmst, fahren, du fährst, and stem changes in vowel-consonant verbs.

topics.topic_en: Präteritum of weak, strong and mixed verbs
topics.term_de: Präteritum der schwachen, starken und gemischten Verben
topics.covers: forming the simple past; sein vs. haben with movement and change of state verbs.
the haben/sein split: sein for movement and change of state, haben otherwise.
the strictly-earlier layer of the past, and why it marks the earlier of two past events.
formation and word order of werden + Infinitiv, and reading it as prediction vs. spoken intention.

topics.topic_en: Modal verbs: conjugation and sentence pattern
topics.covers: the modal + infinitive pattern, and the position of the infinitive when another object follows.
müssen/können/dürfen shift to können/müssen/dürfen plus the bare infinitive in direct speech.
sicher, wohl, vielleicht and the modal + inflected infinitive used as an adverb.
es gibt, es regnet, mir ist kalt: es as a formal placeholder subject.
be-, emp-, ent-, er-, ge-, ver-, zer-: no vowel change, no ge- in the Partizip II.
the prefix in the final field in main clauses, but inside the verb cluster in subordinate clauses.
mir, dir, ihm, ihnen / mich, dich, ihn, sie, es and their order in two-object sentences.
Ich gebe ihm das Buch, and why the shorter dative object comes first.
accusative vs. dative reflexive pronouns, and verbs fixed to one or the other.
du, ihr, Sie and the let-forms, including the position of the pronoun.
case decided by location vs. direction: in, an, auf, über, unter, vor, hinter, neben, zwischen.
aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu, gegenüber.
durch, für, gegen, ohne, um.
des + noun, and the alternative structure with von + Dativ.
topics.split_note: Recognised at B1 by schools and VHS; telc treats Genitive as a full four-case topic from B1.

topics.covers: der Name / der Kollege / das Museum: the full masculine and neuter paradigm with the special plurals.
topics.split_note: Recognition at B1, productive use at B2; telc introduces the full paradigm earlier.

topics.topic_en: Adjective declension after a definite article
topics.covers: weak endings in -e, and -en in the dative plural.

topics.topic_en: Adjective declension after an indefinite or possessive article
topics.term_de: Adjektivdeklination nach unbestimmten Artikeln und Possessiva
topics.covers: mixed endings: -er, -e, -es, -en, and the ein- irregularity.
strong endings, and attributive vs. predicative use.

topics.topic_en: Adjective declension with demonstratives and possessives
topics.covers: dieser/jener/ein jeder and the pattern they share.
-er, am -sten, Gleichstand, and ellipsis in the comparison.
gut → besser → am besten, and where adverb comparison differs from adjective comparison.

topics.topic_en: Participles I and II as adjectives
topics.term_de: Partizip I und II als Adjektiv
topics.covers: das kommende Jahr, das reparierte Auto: participle plus adjective ending.
1.–31., date word order in spoken and written dates.
der/die/das, welcher/welche/welches; case is decided inside the relative clause.

topics.topic_en: Relative clauses: dative, genitive and prepositions
topics.term_de: Relativsätze im Dativ, Genitiv und mit Präpositionen
topics.covers: deren, dessen, and relative pronouns after a preposition.

topics.topic_en: Relative clauses with was, wo, wohin, wann
topics.covers: weil sie Dinge und Personen ersetzen; wo vs. wohin vs. wann.
verb-final, the comma rule, and position I vs. position III.
weil, da, denn, obwohl, trotzdem als Konjunktion.
wenn, als, bevor, nachdem, seit, bis, während.
damit, um zu, zu, sodass, so dass.
which verbs take zu, and the fixed verbs that omit it.
deshalb, trotzdem, außerdem: position zero, then verb in position II.
w-fragen put the verb in position II; yes-no questions put the verb in position I.
ob, wann, wo, wie, warum and the verb-final subordinate clause.
quotation marks, the colon, and pronoun and tense adjustment.
the umlaut + -e forms of sein, haben and the modals.

topics.topic_en: Konjunktiv II: wishes and polite requests
topics.term_de: Konjunktiv II für Wünsche und Höflichkeit
topics.covers: ich würde, gern hätte, könnte ich bitte — the everyday wish and request forms.
würde + haben/sein + Partizip II.

topics.term_de: Konjunktiv II für Ratschläge und Vorschläge
topics.covers: sollte, müsste and thewürde-form for proposing.
wenn + Konjunktiv II and the verb-final position of the wenn-clause.
werden + Partizip II across tenses, and the von-phrase agent.
müssen/sollen/können + werden + Partizip II, and the resulting meanings.

topics.term_de: sein + Partizip II vs. werden + Partizip II
topics.covers: result vs. process, and sein for the resultative reading.

topics.topic_en: Narrating the past: Präteritum vs. Plusquamperfekt
topics.covers: which past tense carries the narrative, and using Plusquamperfekt for the earlier event.
adding Futur II for a future view of the past, and wird + Infinitiv as a present-tense substitute. Futur I itself was covered at B1.
wissen, glauben and modal meaning without an infinitive.
a modal inside a reported clause: Er sagt, er müsse arbeiten.

topics.topic_en: Modal verbs of deduction and hedging
topics.covers: müssen, dürfen, können expressing the speaker's degree of certainty.
the own forms of sein, haben and the modals, and when they replace würde.

topics.topic_en: Konjunktiv II in formal and official requests
topics.covers: escalating politeness for institutional contexts (Ich würde vorschlagen, Wäre es möglich, …); B1 covered everyday wishes and requests.
wenn + Konjunktiv II der Vergangenheit, and wenn vs. als.
als ob, als wenn, als though: unreal resemblance.
an expression for what you hope will not happen.
stem from the infinitive, no umlaut: er habe, er sei, er könne.
topics.split_note: telc's own A1–B1 contents does not list Konjunktiv I, though most B1 coursebooks teach it. Placed at B2 with B1 reported speech as the on-ramp.

topics.covers: er habe gesagt, and the identical 3rd-person-plural form.
topics.split_note: telc omits Konjunktiv I from A1–B1; most other providers place it at B2.

topics.covers: news register: Er behauptet, er habe nichts gewusst.
topics.split_note: Most B1 coursebooks teach reported speech in Konjunktiv I; telc defers it.

topics.covers: the division of labour: distance and official register vs. ordinary report.
topics.split_note: The division of labour is a style rule that providers present at different levels.

topics.covers: reporting verbs and their case: Er sagt, dass... / Er sagt mir, ...

topics.term_de: Wiedergabe von Aufforderungen, Fragen und Gerüchten
topics.covers: Er fragt, ob...; Er sagt, ich solle...; Er sagt, er habe es nicht gewusst.

topics.topic_en: Reported speech with da- and wo- compounds
topics.term_de: indirekte Rede mit da- und wo-
topics.covers: dort, dahin, von wo and the da-/wo- elements.

topics.topic_en: Reported speech with modal verbs in the past
topics.term_de: indirekte Rede mit Modalverben in der Vergangenheit
topics.covers: backshifting the modal as well as the tense inside a reported clause: Er sagte, er müsse gearbeitet haben.
productive Genitive: des Mannes, of people, places and abstract nouns.
topics.split_note: Productive Genitive is placed at B2 here; telc treats it as a B1 topic.

topics.covers: wegen, während, trotz, statt, anhand, hinsichtlich + Genitiv.
sein, deren, dessen and the possessive forms.

topics.topic_en: Adjective and participle as a noun
topics.covers: der Alte, der Deutsche, das Gute, mein Lieber.
turning a verb or adjective into a noun and building genitive chains.
als Vergleich, than-sentences, and je + desto.
determinative and inseparable compounds, and linking elements.

topics.topic_en: The sentence bracket and field positions
topics.covers: position I, II and III, and which constituents can enter the Nachfeld.
nicht vs. kein, placement, and negation scope over a whole clause.
the full set of correlative forms: entweder … oder, nicht nur … sondern auch, sowohl … als auch, weder … noch.
zweiteilige Formen: wenn … auch, obwohl … trotzdem, wie … auch.
falls, sofern, es sei denn, außer wenn, nur dass.
also, folglich, demzufolge, immerhin, schließlich.
denn, weil, deshalb, nämlich and damit vs. um zu.
zuerst, dann, daraufhin, schließlich, inzwischen and their position.
trotzdem, dennoch, allerdings, vielmehr, hingegen.
participle clauses: Ich gehe, ohne mich zu verabschieden.
doch, eben, halt, ja, eben, wohl: position and effect on the mood.
anstatt, um, ohne, anlässlich + zu + Infinitiv.
the compressed subordinate clause: die zur Verfügung stehenden Daten.
topics.split_note: telc and Cornelsen place the Partizipialattribut at B2; Grammatik aktiv marks it B2/C1, so some providers push it to C1.

topics.covers: zu + Partizip I + adjective ending, agreeing with the following noun.

topics.topic_en: Passive alternatives and the agentless passive
topics.covers: sich lassen + Infinitiv, bekommen + Partizip II, and Passiv without an agent.
eine Entscheidung treffen, in Frage kommen, zur Verfügung stellen.
warten auf / helfen bei, and the dependent case that changes.
müsste gemacht werden, and würde + werden + Partizip II.
turning a nominalised phrase back into a clause — the inverse skill for avoiding dense prose.
replacing verbal constructions with nominal ones, the default of written German.
verb → noun derivation, including the stem-vowel change in strong verbs (entscheiden → Entscheidung).
möglich → Möglichkeit, and the fixed adjective→noun conversion.
stacking several nominalisations to pack information into one clause.
long post-nominal participial phrases of the kind that dominate academic German.
subjectless -ender clauses replacing full subordinate clauses.
when the participle hides the agent, and how to reinsert it.
Vorgangspassiv without an agent and without a von-phrase.
sollen and wollen in active and passive signal obligation, not possibility.

topics.topic_en: Modal verbs of speculation in reportage
topics.term_de: subjektive Modalverben und Futur I/II in der Berichterstattung

topics.topic_en: Futur I and Futur II as probability
topics.term_de: Futur I und Futur II für Vermutungen

topics.term_de: Tempus- und Moduswahl in der indirekten Rede

grammatical parallelism and crossed structure for argumentative effect.
placing a heavy element first and the verb second to front information.

multi-step nominal structures as the core resource of high-register prose.
choosing between true passive, man, sich lassen + Infinitiv and bekommen + Partizip II.
